packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - unverified image reading

Exposure / compliance statement
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author for this packet.
- I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..004.jpg in this packet. I did run one directory listing (ls) of my three assigned packet directories to learn the image filenames; packet.json was seen by name only and not read. No web, search or other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001.jpg: reduced overview of one face of a narrow vertical parchment strip, upright, on black felt with a wooden ruler (strip roughly 2.8 cm wide x c. 16 cm tall by the ruler). image-002.jpg: native-resolution crop of the written part of that face.
- image-003.jpg: reduced overview of the other face of the same strip; image-004.jpg: native-resolution crop of its written part.
- The strip is a vertical cut through one text column. Face A (001/002) keeps the LEFT edge of a column (line beginnings, with blank margin to the left; text cut off at right). Face B (003/004) keeps the RIGHT edge of a column (line ends, blank margin to the right; text cut off at left). Only about 5-9 letters survive per line.
- Upper third of the strip is blank on both faces (upper margin; a slit/sewing mark and a fold line run vertically). Face B has a darker brown rectangular stain (paste/offset) at the top.
- Script: large formal gothic bookhand (textualis), black ink, widely spaced lines; 16 black lines visible on face A plus one line in red at the foot; 16-17 lines on face B.
- Red: on face A, initials touched/stroked in red at line 4 (a red capital, cut by the edge) and line 7 ("Et" with red stroke); the last visible line (17) is written wholly in red = a rubric (observation). No running title, no glosses, no underlining visible. No large decorated initial survives.
- Tentative interpretation only: single text with rubrics, written in long lines or columns of a large-format book; column count cannot be determined from a strip this narrow.

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
- Everything visible on both faces was read (all lines). Nothing more can be obtained from these crops; each line is a fragment of a few letters, so no connected ten-line prose span exists on this leaf. A neighbouring strip from the same leaf would be needed for continuous text.

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE A (image-002.jpg; same lines visible reduced in image-001.jpg, not additional text)
Line beginnings; each line is cut off at the right "[".
image-002 l.1   ter intr[
image-002 l.2   et perue[   (4th-6th letters: "p" with stroke + "ue"/"ne"; "perue" or "perne"?)
image-002 l.3   autē (autem) m[   (after "autē" minims: "m" / "in"?)
image-002 l.4   bisset  C[   (red capital, cut; C or E?)
image-002 l.5   turion[   ("turione"/"turioni"; ending cut)
image-002 l.6   cum si[
image-002 l.7   set  Et c[   ("Et" touched red; next letter c or o?)
image-002 l.8   a centu[   (read "a centu"; minims after "cent" uncertain: "centur"?)
image-002 l.9   corpus
image-002 l.10  tem mo[   ("tem m" certain, following letter o?)
image-002 l.11  et depon[   ("et depo" then one or two cut letters: "depon"/"depos"?)
image-002 l.12  syndone[   ("s" + y with dot + "ndone"; final letter at the cut)
image-002 l.13  monum[   ("monum" + minims)
image-002 l.14  excisum?[   (ex + c/a + tall letter + minims; "excisu(m)"? very uncertain in the middle - could be "exalum")
image-002 l.15  uoluit?[   (initial u/n, "olu" + minims/e; "uoluit" / "uolute"?)
image-002 l.16  ium mo[   (minims "ium"/"uim"/"num" then "mo"; a hole follows)
image-002 l.17  RED: debet? sa[   (rubric, pale red, lower half cut by the foot of the strip; "debet" or "debes"? then "sa"/"fa"/"sau"?)

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE B (image-004.jpg; same lines reduced in image-003.jpg)
Line ends; each line is cut off at the left "]".
image-004 l.1   ]nō (non) erat   ("erat" - or "eiat"? reading "erat" preferred)
image-004 l.2   ]elum et   ("]elu" + minim(s): "celum"? first letter cut)
image-004 l.3   ] dignā (dignam?) et   (could also be read "dignaet"/"dignat(ur)"? - mark over a uncertain)
image-004 l.4   ]cti bea   ("]ctī"/"]cti" with a descending stroke - possibly "s(an)cti"?; then "bea")
image-004 l.5   ] digna
image-004 l.6   ]mata?   (minims + "ata": "]mata"/"]nata"/"]luata"?)
image-004 l.7   ]agnum?   ("]a" + d/g + "num": "]agnum" / "]adnum"?)
image-004 l.8   ]laudem
image-004 l.9   ]s que
image-004 l.10  ]dn̄s (dominus) de⁹ (deus)   (first word abraded: "dns" with stroke; "de" with superscript -us sign)
image-004 l.11  ]rtas fa   ("]rtas" or "]ctas"?)
image-004 l.12  ]ro tuo   ("]ro" then "tuo"; a faint mark above t)
image-004 l.13  ]ueloc̄? / ]uelocit(er)?   ("ue loc" + final letter with abbreviation stroke; "uelocit(er)"?)
image-004 l.14  ]aluū (saluum?) me   ("]aluū" with stroke over final u; initial letter cut)
image-004 l.15  ]ī ir(?)itaue?   (very uncertain: "]i" + stroke, then i/c + r/u + "itaue"/"itatē"; could be "ciuitate"?)
image-004 l.16  ]m? aicum?   (smudged; "]... a" + tall letter + "um"; not securely readable)
image-004 l.17  [illegible - only tops of letters at the cut foot of the strip]

LIMITATIONS
- Both faces are a strip c. 2.8 cm wide: every line is truncated on one side, so word divisions and expansions at the cut edges are guesses and are marked as such.
- Face B is rubbed and stained (brown offset); lines 6-7 and 15-17 are the weakest.
- Which face is recto and which verso is not determinable from the images.
- Suggest: a wider view is impossible (this is the whole strip), but any sister strips from the same binding would give the adjoining letters.
